headline: Lānaʻi commission backs farm subdivision notice bill on second vote

meeting.summary: The commission approved a farm subdivision notice bill on a second vote and reviewed a permit for a private Four Seasons event.
meeting.recap: The commission held a public hearing on a County Council bill about farm land subdivisions.[[0:02:46]] Owners would have to notify lessees (people renting the land) by certified mail at least 10 business days before applying.[[0:08:25]] The Planning Department recommended moving the rule to Title 18, the County's subdivision code.[[0:12:31]] A motion to approve the bill with that change got four votes, but five were needed.[[0:39:37]] A motion to defer the bill died without a second.[[0:40:27]] A second motion to approve the bill with the department's change carried unanimously.[[0:52:01]] Commissioners asked that the council also consider notice for residential and commercial land.[[0:55:29]] The department brought a permit for a private event at the Four Seasons luau grounds on October 10th.[[0:57:03]] Staff said no formal vote was needed because a rule change is not yet official.[[0:59:22]] A commissioner said beach park rangers cannot enforce rules on the event's music and lighting.[[1:16:17]] A hotel representative said music at its events shuts down at 10 p.m.[[1:17:02]] The department said it plans to approve the permit.[[1:39:03]] The next meeting is October 21st.[[1:46:51]]
decided: The first motion to approve got four votes and did not pass because five were needed.
A motion to defer the bill to get more information from the council died because no one seconded it.
The commission voted to recommend approval of the bill with the department's recommended amendments.
meeting.next: The bill goes to the Molokaʻi Planning Commission next week. Staff will take all three planning commissions' recommendations to the council before it decides.
